info.name: IPC
info.description:
Complete route catalogue and response-contract tests for the current Kotlin backend, including all supported aliases. Examples are synthetic.

SETUP: Choose serverDomainName (local by default). Register/login test accounts and log in separately as patient, physiotherapist and administrator; each Login response stores the corresponding id/token/refresh variables by role. Fill loginEmail/loginPassword before each login. Registration requires newAccountPassword and unique new*Email values. Credentials approval and patient/physiotherapist connection must exist before prescription tests. Administrator creation requires an existing administrator token. Choose local files for all multipart uploads.

EXECUTION: Create a plan (stores template planID), assign it to idPatient, then fetch the patient plan for date. That response stores assignedPlanID, dailyListID, dailyexerciseID and prescribedReps. Never substitute template IDs for assignment IDs. Fetch the effective profile before submitting a sensor session. sensorSessionId is generated only when blank: keep it AND the payload unchanged for an idempotent retry; clear it when switching to a new set/assignment. sensorSet=1 and cameraSet=2 avoid occupying the same set in both modes; the fixture must prescribe at least two sets. Feedback uses set. Empty date is initialized to today's UTC date.

RUNNING: Run selected requests/folders against prepared test fixtures. This is a route catalogue, not a single automatic end-to-end provisioning sequence: aliases repeat mutations, registration requires unique emails, request rejection/connection deletion need separate fixtures, and media require files. Do not run the entire catalogue blindly against existing application data. Supported aliases are tested with the same contracts as canonical routes. Negative tests require valid role tokens and a valid assignment so they test the intended failure.

SSE: Streaming is skipped by default to avoid blocking the Runner; set runStreaming=true and send the subscription manually. Unsubscribe closes the authenticated user's stream. SSE assertions run only when the response completes.

Assertions validate exact success status, JSON schemas, empty 204 responses, media types, profile invariants, session echo and explicit 400/403/404 cases. No production requests were executed when updating this collection.

request.description:
Backend route: `GET /users/subscribe`

Long-lived SSE connection for the authenticated user. Response Content-Type: text/event-stream. Send Accept: */* (or application/json, as the Android app does): the current controller declares JSON/image media types, so an exclusive Accept: text/event-stream can be rejected during Spring route negotiation. The event id is the emitter class name; JSON data includes RequestPhysiotherapist, RequestAcceptance, PostedVideo, PhysiotherapistFeedBack, PlanAssociation, CredentialAcceptance and RatePhysiotherapist. An initial acceptance event is sent. Open manually or opt in using runStreaming in Postman; normal Runner execution skips this indefinite stream. Authorization: authenticated user; ownership/relationship checks apply where relevant.

exec: if (pm.variables.get("runStreaming") !== "true") { console.info("SSE skipped. Set runStreaming=true and send manually to open the stream."); pm.execution.skipRequest(); }
